q: A train is coming. How far from the nearest rail or gate must you stop?
a: At least 5 metres
e: Stop at least 5 m from the nearest rail or gate.
s: If a train is coming, stop at least five metres from the nearest rail or gate.

q: You're coming up behind a school bus with its red lights flashing. How far back must you stop?
a: At least 20 metres
e: From behind, stop at least 20 m back.
s: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.

q: You must not pass any vehicle within how many metres of a pedestrian crossover?
a: 30 metres
e: No passing within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover.
s: You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

q: Under full emergency braking, how far can it take a train to stop?
a: Up to 2 kilometres
e: Trains can't stop quickly. Never race a train.
s: Remember it can take up to two kilometres for a train to stop under full emergency braking.

q: A school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing on an undivided road. You're coming toward it from the front. What must you do?
a: Stop
w: Keep going; only traffic behind it must stop
e: On a road without a median, traffic from both directions must stop.
s: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on the other side of a road with a median. You're coming toward it from the front. Must you stop?
a: No: on a road with a median, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop
w: Yes, but only during school hours
Only if children are in the road
e: A median is a physical divider you can't drive over. Still watch carefully for children.
s: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

q: A school bus ahead has its overhead AMBER lights flashing. What does it mean, and what should you do?
a: It's about to stop: slow down and prepare to stop
w: Stop right away, even if it's far ahead
e: Amber = getting ready to stop. Red = stopped: you must stop.
s: Slow down and prepare to stop whether you are behind or approaching the bus

q: You're stopped for a school bus with red lights flashing. When may you go?
a: When the bus moves, or the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm folds away
w: When the children are on the sidewalk
When the bus driver waves at you
e: Wait for the bus to move or the lights and stop arm to go off.
s: Remain stopped until the arm folds away and all lights stop flashing.

q: A school crossing guard is holding up a stop sign. The children have crossed your lane, but the guard is still in the road. What do you do?
a: Stay stopped until everyone, including the guard, has cleared the whole road
w: Go once the children pass your lane
Honk to tell the guard to move
e: Wait until all people, including the guard, have cleared the entire roadway.
s: you must stop before reaching the crossing and remain stopped until all people, including the school crossing guard, have cleared the entire roadway

q: A pedestrian at a crossover has passed your lane and is now in the far lane. When may you go?
a: Only when they have completely crossed the road
w: Now, since they're out of your lane
When they reach the centre line
When the overhead lights stop flashing
e: At a crossover, wait until the pedestrian is safely on the sidewalk.
s: Only when pedestrians and school crossing guards have crossed and are safely on the sidewalk can drivers and cyclists proceed.

q: The railway crossing lights are still flashing, but the train has passed and the gate is going up. What do you do?
a: Wait until the lights stop flashing and the gate is all the way up
w: Go as soon as the gate starts rising
Go around the gate since the train is gone
Go if you can see no second train
e: Never drive under or around a gate that is down, being lowered or being raised.
s: If there are signal lights, wait until they stop flashing and, if the crossing has a gate or barrier, wait until it rises before you cross the tracks.

q: In the lane beside you, a car is stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?
a: Don't pass it: a pedestrian may be crossing in front of it
e: A stopped vehicle at a crosswalk may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.
s: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

q: You're driving behind a school bus that is approaching a railway crossing. What should you expect?
a: The bus will stop at the crossing, without using its red lights, so be ready to stop behind it
w: The bus will speed up to cross
The bus will flash its red lights and stop arm
The bus will pull onto the shoulder
e: All school buses must stop at all railway crossings. They don't use the upper red lights for these stops.
s: All school buses must stop at all railway crossings. The upper alternating red lights are not used for these stops, so be alert.

q: When does the school bus law apply?
a: On any road, any number of lanes, any speed limit, at any time of day
w: Only on roads with a speed limit under 80 km/h
e: Be prepared to stop for a school bus at any time, not just during school hours.
s: You must obey the school bus law on any road, no matter how many lanes or what the speed limit. Be prepared to stop for a school bus at any time, not just within school hours.

q: When is it legal to drive around, under or through a railway crossing gate?
a: Never while it is down, being lowered or being raised
w: When you can see no train coming
When the gate is only halfway down
When you're in a hurry and the crossing is clear
e: Going around a railway barrier is illegal and dangerous (3 demerit points).
s: Never drive around, under or through a railway gate or barrier while it is down, being lowered or being raised.

q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a divided road with a median. You're BEHIND the bus. Must you stop?
a: Yes: traffic behind the bus must stop, even on a road with a median
w: No, the median means nobody has to stop
Only if you're in the right lane
Only if children are getting off
e: The median only frees the traffic coming the other way.
s: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

q: Which vehicles must stop at EVERY railway crossing, even ones with gates or signal lights?
a: School buses
e: Most buses stop at unprotected crossings. School buses stop at every crossing.
s: School buses must stop at railway crossings whether or not they are protected by gates or signal lights.

q: You come to a railway crossing on a quiet country road. There are no gates or lights. What should you do?
a: Slow down, listen, and look both ways to make sure the way is clear before crossing
w: Cross at your normal speed; trains always use lights
Stop on the tracks to look both ways
e: Not every crossing has gates or lights. Never stop on the tracks themselves.
s: Slow down, listen and look both ways to make sure the way is clear before crossing the tracks.

q: Your car stalls on the railway tracks. What should you do FIRST?
a: Get everyone out and away from the car, then call for help
w: Stay inside with your seatbelt on
Push the car off the tracks
e: Get everyone to a safe place first, then contact authorities.
s: If you get trapped on a crossing, immediately get everyone out and away from the vehicle. Move to a safe place and then contact authorities.

q: Traffic is heavy and backed up across the railway tracks ahead. What should you do?
a: Wait until there's room to get completely across the tracks before you start
w: Follow the car ahead onto the tracks
Stop on the tracks; traffic will move soon
Cross the tracks in the oncoming lane
e: Never stop on the tracks.
s: Avoid stopping in the middle of railway tracks; for example, in heavy traffic, make sure you have enough room to cross the tracks completely before you begin.

q: You're driving a car with a manual transmission over railway tracks. What should you avoid?
a: Shifting gears while crossing the tracks
e: Shifting on the tracks could stall the car.
s: Avoid shifting gears while crossing tracks.

q: A railway crossing has a stop sign. What must you do?
a: Stop, unless a flagman directs you otherwise
w: Stop only if a train is visible
e: A stop sign at a railway crossing means stop.
s: If you are approaching a railway crossing with a stop sign, you must stop unless otherwise directed by a flagman.

q: A driver passes a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing, and a witness reports the car. Who can be fined?
a: The vehicle's registered owner (fines only, not demerit points or jail)
w: No one, unless police saw it
The witness, for not stopping the car
e: School bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that illegally pass a school bus.
s: If you are the vehicle’s registered owner, these fines, but not demerit points or jail time, may be applied to you.
